A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work with complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendix A. All 27 pages were compared; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its associated link.

before.justification: v2 reports original continuous-control simulations, including five-seed performance comparisons, learning curves, stability analyses, and energy estimates in Section 5 and Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original simulation results in Section 5 and Appendix A.6, including performance comparisons across five MuJoCo environments.

M1.justification: The continuous proxy target, imitation loss, gradient-based updates, and spiking actor architecture are identical, including Equations 6–8 and Algorithms 1–3.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five MuJoCo tasks: InvertedDoublePendulum-v4, Ant-v4, HalfCheetah-v4, Hopper-v4, and Walker2d-v4. No training or evaluation scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ANN (TD3), ANN–SNN conversion, vanilla LIF, pop-SAN, MDC-SAN, and ILC-SAN. Comparator membership in the corresponding appendix experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A.4 retain identical TD3 settings, preprocessing, architectures, hyperparameters, and evaluation metrics, including the default five SNN simulation steps.

E4.justification: The target-output and alignment analyses in Figure 2, stability analysis in Figure 6(a), and ANN control experiments in Figure 6(b) and Appendix A.6.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report five random seeds, one-standard-deviation uncertainty in Table 1, and half-standard-deviation shading in Figures 5 and 8. Statistical reporting practices are identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, both report PT-LIF's 5.84% average performance gain against ANN in Table 1 and 32.15% against vanilla LIF in Table 8.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its continuous-differentiability assumption and Taylor-expansion proof in Appendix A.1, and the mathematical definitions and derivations are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same mismatch diagnosis, proxy-target contributions, up-to-32% performance claim, and claim that simple LIF networks surpass ANN performance without additional inference overhead.

C2.justification: Interpretations of target smoothing, simple-neuron performance, and SNN-specific benefits are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation that evaluation remains at the simulation level.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.5 retain identical pseudocode, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and preprocessing information. The stated code repository and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning relative to previous SNN learning rules and hybrid actor–critic frameworks are identical.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v2, dated 23 October 2025, to v3, dated 2 February 2026. Manuscript wording, terminology, headings, and section order are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–11, algorithm displays, captions, and body layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–27 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the existing margin stamp's text.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and associated link produces no meaningful change in overall paper quality.
